analysis.investment_thesis: Borosil Renewables is India's only solar glass manufacturer riding the renewable energy wave, but Chinese import competition has systematically destroyed margins — EBITDA collapsed from ₹256 Cr in FY22 to ₹73 Cr in FY25 despite revenue nearly doubling to ₹1,476 Cr. At 73x P/E on actual losses of -₹87 Cr, the market is pricing in a government-protection-led turnaround that has not materialized.
key_strengths: India's only domestic solar glass manufacturer — structural moat if government imposes meaningful BCD on solar glass imports
Revenue CAGR of ~18% over a decade (₹156 Cr to ₹1,476 Cr) shows real demand capture despite pricing headwinds
Promoter holding stable at 58.77% and Debt/Equity low at 0.23 with debt correcting from ₹576 Cr peak (FY24) to ₹252 Cr (FY25)
key_risks: Chinese solar glass overcapacity is destroying unit economics — operating income flat at ₹58 Cr in FY25 on ₹1,476 Cr revenue (~4% margin) vs. ₹223 Cr on ₹642 Cr revenue (~35%) in FY22
ROE of -8.9% and ROCE of -4.4% — capital destruction, not creation; net losses of ₹50 Cr (FY24) and ₹87 Cr (FY25) are accelerating
FCF has been negative in 4 of 5 years (FY25: -₹8 Cr, FY24: -₹148 Cr) with heavy capex; business is not self-funding
red_flags: P/E of 73.3x is reported against a company posting net losses of -₹87 Cr — valuation is entirely speculative/forward-looking with no earnings support
Finance costs surged from ₹3 Cr (FY22) to ₹32 Cr (FY25) as debt ballooned to fund capex, squeezing an already thin bottom line
EBITDA margin compression from ~40% (FY22) to ~5% (FY25) despite revenue growth signals structural margin erosion, not cyclical
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Borosil Renewables has the right India thesis — it is the sole domestic manufacturer of solar glass in a country targeting 500 GW of solar capacity by 2030. The PLI and Make in India narrative is compelling, and the promoter (Borosil Group) has a respectable track record. Revenue growth from ₹642 Cr (FY22) to ₹1,476 Cr (FY25) shows the company is winning volume. But volume without profitability is a treadmill, not a business. Chinese manufacturers dumping low-cost solar glass have effectively neutralized Borosil's domestic advantage — EBITDA has collapsed from ₹256 Cr to ₹73 Cr over the same period, and net profit has swung from +₹166 Cr to -₹87 Cr. This is not a growth company at this moment; it is a distressed manufacturing business hoping for policy rescue.

As a Jhunjhunwala-style investor, I need both the story AND the numbers. The story here is intact — India needs domestic solar supply chains. But the numbers are alarming: negative returns on capital, accelerating losses, five consecutive years of negative FCF, and a stock priced at 73x on zero real earnings. The only scenario for buying this stock is if the government imposes protective import duties on solar glass (like it did for modules). Until that policy trigger materializes, every rupee invested is funding losses and speculative hope. I do not pay 73x for hope. At ₹498, this stock is significantly overvalued for its current fundamentals. Wait for either a deep correction (₹150-200 range) or a clear government tariff notification before considering entry.
